opening_message:
Ticket 1: Maurice Perez (employee ID E036) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E036.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Maurice Perez (E036) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write, so write is within policy. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Maurice Perez (E036) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max out at read without advanced training, so write exceeds policy. Recommend read.
reason: The two team notes conflict on employment type: HR note says full-time Engineer (max write), but Security note says contractor with basic security training (max read). Given the unresolved conflict, I apply the more restrictive and conservative level. Per policy, a contractor with basic training may not exceed read, so granting write would violate policy if the security record is correct. Grant read.
